impact.affected_asset: Linux kernel memory and execution context associated with a SocketCAN ISO-TP socket.
impact.attacker_capability: A local low-privileged attacker able to exercise the relevant ISO-TP socket and device-unregistration lifecycle can target the documented teardown race; exploitation reliability is not established by the bundle.
impact.security_effect: Vendor-reported local privilege escalation and arbitrary code execution in kernel context through a socket timer use-after-free.

causal_trace.summary: NETDEV_UNREGISTER causes isotp_notify() to unregister RCU CAN receive filters and clear so->bound without first waiting for a grace period.
isotp_release() uses so->bound to decide whether to synchronize RCU; after isotp_notify() clears that flag, release can skip synchronization although an isotp_rcv() reader remains in flight.
The in-flight isotp_rcv() can call isotp_send_fc() and re-arm so->rxtimer after release cancels it, leaving a timer callback associated with a freed socket.

The later timer callback is described by the upstream patch as a use-after-free callback on the freed socket; the coordinated disclosure reports resulting kernel-context arbitrary code execution and local privilege escalation.

failure.operation: Use-after-free timer callback on a freed ISO-TP socket after an in-flight receive callback re-arms rxtimer.

primary_invariant.kind: RCU-protected socket teardown and timer lifetime
primary_invariant.statement: Before so->bound is cleared in isotp_notify(), in-flight isotp_rcv() callbacks must quiesce so that isotp_release() cannot bypass its RCU wait while a callback can re-arm so->rxtimer.
primary_invariant.violated_because: CAN-filter unregistration was followed by clearing so->bound without synchronize_rcu(), allowing release to observe the cleared state, skip synchronization, and race an in-flight receiver that re-arms the timer.

quality.review_notes: The upstream patch gives a specific causal interleaving and remediation, and the coordinated disclosure supplies scope and impact claims. No bundled reproducer, runtime crash/KASAN evidence, test result, merged-fix reference, complete affected-version range, or public exploit reliability evidence establishes deterministic reproduction or exploitation.

remediation.invariant_restored: isotp_notify() waits for in-flight isotp_rcv() callers after unregistering CAN filters and before clearing so->bound, preserving isotp_release()'s synchronization decision and preventing the callback/timer re-arm interleaving.
mitigation_classes: RCU reader quiescence before state transition

state_context.attacker_state_setup: The disclosure requires local low-privileged code. The supplied material does not provide a standalone trigger sequence for causing the netdevice-unregistration, release, and receive-callback ordering.
data_structure_invariants: so->bound must not be cleared so early that isotp_release() skips required RCU synchronization while isotp_rcv() remains active.
so->rxtimer must not be re-armed by an in-flight callback after socket release has cancelled it and freed the socket.
state_context.state_machine: NETDEV_UNREGISTER enters isotp_notify(), which unregisters receive filters; pre-fix it clears bound state before reader quiescence. Socket release consults that state to decide whether to wait for RCU readers, while an already-running receive callback can re-arm the receive timer.
